slides.title: Respect Looks Different in Different Settings
slides.content: Respect applies: In college. On industry placement. Online. In future workplaces. College expects students to increasingly self-regulate and behave professionally.

slides.title: The PROUD Values
slides.content: These are the core ESCG values: Create a welcoming and supportive environment. Treat everyone fairly and appropriately. Take opportunities to learn and develop. Work positively with others and challenge exclusion. Value differences and recognise that diversity strengthens the community.

slides.title: British Values
slides.content: The four British Values are: Students can influence college through elections, surveys and feedback. College rules and UK law apply to everyone. People can make their own choices, provided they do not harm others. Everyone deserves fair treatment regardless of background.

slides.title: The Equality Act 2010
slides.content: The Equality Act protects people from discrimination based on nine protected characteristics: 1. Age 2. Disability 3. Gender reassignment 4. Marriage and civil partnership 5. Pregnancy and maternity 6. Race 7. Religion or belief 8. Sex 9. Sexual orientation

slides.title: Important Equality Act Terms
slides.content: Discrimination: Treating someone unfairly because of a protected characteristic. Harassment: Unwanted behaviour that creates a hostile or offensive environment. Victimisation: Treating someone unfairly because they raised or supported a concern about discrimination.

slides.title: Behaviour Standards
slides.content: The same standards apply: In college. On placement. Online. Key expectations: Respectful language. No bullying or harassment. No discriminatory behaviour. Responsible use of technology. No recording or sharing content without permission. Professional conduct on placements.

slides.title: Your Digital Footprint Matters
slides.content: Remember: Online content can be permanent. Employers may see your online activity. Social media behaviour can have college consequences. College policies can apply to online conduct.

slides.title: Zero Tolerance
slides.content: ESCG has zero tolerance for: Harassment. Discrimination. Bullying. Abuse. Serious consequences can include: Formal disciplinary procedures. Suspension. Permanent exclusion.

slides.title: How to Report Concerns
slides.content: There are three reporting routes: 1. Tell your teacher. 2. Use the formal reporting system. 3. Use anonymous reporting. All concerns are taken seriously.
